items.title: A finitely punctured open disk has the homotopy type of a finite wedge of circles
items.statement: For each finite set Q of k distinct interior points, int D² minus Q is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of k circles, with one positively oriented meridian per puncture as a free basis of π₁. It has π_j=0 for every j≥2. For k=0 the wedge is a point. The same conclusions hold for C minus k points under the explicit radial homeomorphism C≅int D². No choice axiom is used.
items.proof_strategy: Choose a smaller closed disk enclosing Q and pairwise disjoint small disks around the punctures. Radially retract the outside collar to the smaller disk and each puncture neighborhood to its small boundary circle. Choose finite noncrossing arcs from those circles to a common outer-boundary base arc. Cutting along the arcs leaves a disk; collapse that disk across collars to the graph of the k meridian circles and stems, then contract the stem tree to a wedge of k circles. Give the deformation on each cut disk and collar, checking that the pieces agree on their common edges; k=0 contracts radially. The published wedge theorem identifies its π₁ and meridian basis. Construct its covering graph with vertices reduced words on k letters and one labelled edge for each appended letter; local star neighborhoods cover the wedge, and unique reduced paths make the graph a tree. Contract a tree toward its root along unique finite edge paths (continuity is checked on each finite subgraph). For j≥2, S^j is simply connected, so the covering lifting criterion lifts every based sphere map; contract it upstairs and project the nullhomotopy, using homotopy lifting to identify based nullhomotopies. Homotopy equivalence transfers π₁ and π_j. Finally z↦z/(1+|z|) identifies C with int D² and carries finite puncture sets across.

items.title: Vanishing π₂ for every ordered planar configuration space
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1 and every base configuration, π₂(F_n(int D²))=0; the same holds for F_n(C) and F_n(D²) via the explicit plane/open-disk homeomorphism and the published open-to-closed configuration equivalence.
items.proof_strategy: Use AC exactly to obtain DC and invoke part 3 of the published Fadell–Neuwirth theorem: forgetting the last point in the open disk is a Hurewicz, hence Serre, fibration with punctured-disk fiber. Its base F₁(int D²)=int D² is contractible by radial homotopy, so π₂ vanishes at n=1. For n≥2 the LES segment π₂(fiber)→π₂(F_n)→π₂(F_{n−1}) is exact. The first group is zero by the preceding punctured-disk lemma and the last by induction, forcing the middle group zero. This induction precedes every assertion that the fiber π₁ injects into PB_n. Apply the explicit coordinatewise C≅int D² homeomorphism and the published open-to-closed homotopy equivalence for the two other models.

items.title: The Fadell–Neuwirth short exact sequence for pure braids
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥2, forgetting the last strand yields a short exact sequence 1→F_{n−1}→PB_n→PB_{n−1}→1, where F_{n−1}=π₁(int D² minus {q₁,…,q_{n−1}},q_n) is free on the n−1 puncture meridians and the left map is induced by inclusion of the fiber. PB₁ is trivial. The PB groups use the published closed-disk convention and are compared to the open-disk sequence by the published inclusion isomorphisms.
items.proof_strategy: Under AC derive DC and use the published Hurewicz fibration for p:F_n(int D²)→F_{n−1}(int D²). At q the fiber is int D² minus n−1 fixed points. The preceding spine lemma supplies its connectedness and its free π₁ basis. In the LES, π₂(F_{n−1})=0 by the preceding simultaneous induction, so the boundary into π₁(fiber) is zero and fiber inclusion on π₁ is injective. Connectedness of the fiber makes the following π₁(p) surjective, giving exactness and rank n−1. Use the published open-to-closed inclusion isomorphisms at q, and their compatibility with coordinate forgetting, to transport the sequence to the fixed PB_n notation. Check n=2 directly from PB₁=1 and one meridian; no group action or Artin-presentation injectivity is used.

items.title: Point pushing is the kernel of forgetting the last disk puncture
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥2. The point-pushing homomorphism Push_n:π₁(int D² minus {q₁,…,q_{n−1}},q_n)→PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) is injective, and its image is exactly the kernel of the homomorphism that forgets the last marked point PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²)→PMod(D²,Q_{n−1};∂D²). Thus 1→F_{n−1}→PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²)→PMod(D²,Q_{n−1};∂D²)→1 is exact.
items.proof_strategy: First use the previous short exact sequence to prove that the inclusion of the last-point fiber in F_n(int D²) induces an injection on π₁ and has image ker(p_*); its proof uses the newly established π₂(F_{n−1})=0. For a fiber loop hold q₁,…,q_{n−1} fixed, pass to the unordered configuration loop and lift its point motion in the boundary-fixed homeomorphism evaluation bundle. The batch-20 definition applies the inverse-endpoint boundary, so this transported map is precisely Push_n, with its first-then-second multiplication convention. Check the square with the two evaluation-boundary isomorphisms by forgetting the final coordinate of each lifted point-motion path; this identifies p_* with forgetting the last puncture on pure mapping classes. Transport injection, kernel equality and surjectivity through the published pure braid/mapping-class isomorphisms. No Birman injectivity is used to prove the preceding π₂ lemma.

items.title: A choice-free continuous section of planar coordinate forgetting
items.statement: For n≥2, the projection F_n(C)→F_{n−1}(C) has an explicit continuous section. Transporting it through the coordinatewise homeomorphism C≅int D² gives a section of F_n(int D²)→F_{n−1}(int D²). For any specified configuration q, a path in its punctured last-point fiber connects q_n to the section value, so the section yields a based π₁ splitting after that basepoint adjustment. The construction uses no choice axiom.
items.proof_strategy: Define R(z₁,…,z_{n−1})=1+Σ_i|z_i| and s(z)=(z₁,…,z_{n−1},R(z)). The last coordinate is a positive real number of modulus strictly larger than every |z_i|, so no collision occurs; the finite sum is continuous and forgetting it gives the identity. The explicit radial homeomorphism h(w)=w/(1+|w|) and inverse h^{-1}(u)=u/(1−|u|) carry the section to the open disk. At a prescribed base q the last-point fiber is path connected by the punctured-disk spine lemma; choose one path from q_n to s(q₁,…,q_{n−1}) and use the standard path-conjugation basepoint map to obtain a based section. No simultaneous family of such paths is selected, and the explicit section itself needs neither the fibration theorem nor AC.

items.title: The pure braid extension splits as a semidirect product
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥2. A based version of the continuous section induces a homomorphism PB_{n−1}→PB_n right inverse to forgetting, hence PB_n≅F_{n−1}⋊PB_{n−1}. The action is conjugation through the chosen section and depends on that section; no trivial action or direct-product assertion is made.
items.proof_strategy: Choose the single path in the fiber from the inherited q_n to the explicit section value as in the preceding choice-free lemma. Apply π₁ to the section at its natural basepoint and conjugate by that path to obtain a homomorphism at q whose composite with p_* is the identity; the path projects to a constant path, so no base conjugacy remains downstairs. The preceding short exact sequence and the published splitting criterion yield F_{n−1}⋊PB_{n−1}; define its action as x↦s(g)xs(g)^{-1} on the free kernel. AC appears only because the published fibration supplies the short exact sequence, not in the explicit section.

items.title: Ordered planar configuration spaces are aspherical
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1, every k≥2 and every basepoint, π_k(F_n(int D²))=0. The same holds for F_n(C) by the radial plane/disk homeomorphism and for F_n(D²) by the published homotopy equivalence. Thus the ordered open-disk and plane configuration spaces are K(PB_n,1) in the higher-homotopy sense.
items.proof_strategy: The k=2 assertion is the separately proved simultaneous-induction lemma; do not use any short exact point-pushing statement for it. For fixed k≥3, apply the published disk forgetful fibration under AC and the AC⇒DC theorem. The LES segment π_k(fiber)→π_k(F_n)→π_k(F_{n−1})→π_{k−1}(fiber) has both fiber groups zero by the punctured-disk spine lemma, so the middle map is an isomorphism. Iterate to F₁(int D²), which contracts radially, to make π_k(F_n)=0. The explicit plane/open-disk homeomorphism and published open/closed equivalence carry the conclusion to the other models; the published PB_n definition identifies π₁, without assuming that a generic K(π,1) fundamental group must be torsion-free.

items.title: Unordered planar configuration spaces are aspherical
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1 and k≥2, π_k(C_n(int D²))=0, and likewise for C_n(C) and C_n(D²). In particular the open-disk and plane unordered configuration spaces are K(B_n^{conf},1) in the higher-homotopy sense.
items.proof_strategy: The published regular covering F_n(int D²)→C_n(int D²) has path-connected total and base. For k≥2, S^k is simply connected, so the covering lifting criterion lifts every based sphere map from the unordered space to the ordered space. Its class is zero by ordered asphericity, and projecting a based nullhomotopy gives surjectivity of the zero assertion. Conversely homotopy lifting makes the cover induce an isomorphism on π_k: lift any nullhomotopy with its specified initial lift and compare endpoints using uniqueness, taking care of the basepoint. Apply the coordinatewise plane/disk homeomorphism and the published unordered open-to-closed equivalence. The published configuration braid definition supplies the π₁ label; it is not used to prove higher-homotopy vanishing.

items.title: Standard geometric pure braid generators A_ij
items.statement: For 1≤i<j≤n, let A_ij be the geometric pure braid represented, with first-under-second stacking, by σ_{j−1}⋯σ_{i+1} σ_i² σ_{i+1}^{−1}⋯σ_{j−1}^{−1}. Its endpoint permutation is the identity. Here σ_r denotes the published positive geometric half twist, or the image of the same letter under the published Artin-to-geometric surjection; no injectivity or completeness of that presentation is asserted. The definition is choice-free.
items.proof_strategy: Interpret the displayed word through the already constructed surjection and first-under-second stacking. The outer braid moves label j adjacent to label i, σ_i² returns each of these two labels to its start, and the inverse outer braid returns every displaced label. Multiplying endpoint permutations gives identity, so the published pure-geometric/ordered-configuration identification places A_ij in PB_n. For j=i+1 the product is σ_i². This fixes the conjugation order by geometric motion and never identifies the abstract Artin group with the geometric group by an unproved isomorphism.

items.title: The A_in are meridian generators of the forgetful free kernel
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥2. Under the fiber-inclusion identification F_{n−1}≅ker(PB_n→PB_{n−1}), the elements Ψ([A_{1n}]),…,Ψ([A_{n−1,n}]) are a free basis. There is a compatible system of pairwise interior-disjoint stems from q_n to small circles around q_1,…,q_{n−1} such that, for the counterclockwise based meridian γ_i along the i-th stem, Ψ([A_{in}])=(κ_*[γ_i])^{-1}; thus these generators are the clockwise based meridians under the published inverse-loop convention.
items.proof_strategy: Use AC⇒DC and the Fadell–Neuwirth exact sequence to identify the free fiber kernel. For each adjacent pair, identify F₂(U_i) with S¹×C, where C is the convex space of midpoint and separation-length coordinates. The explicit positive half-twist squared has relative winding +1, as does moving q_{i+1} along a local stem, once counterclockwise around q_i, and back; the inverse-loop and inverse-endpoint conventions therefore identify Ψ([A_{i,i+1}]) with the clockwise meridian. Conjugation by H_{n−1}⋯H_{i+1} transports these point-pushes and their endpoint-fixed stem classes. Inductively reroute the transported stems inside the puncture-free support lens to a compatible disjoint fan, then attach each next local stem in a sector avoiding the old fan. A regular neighborhood of the fan and its circles is a disk with holes; radial retractions of the inner punctured disks and outer collar reduce the fiber to this neighborhood, whose tree-and-circles spine gives the stated meridian basis. The inverse of a free basis is again a free basis; no Artin-presentation injectivity is used.

items.title: All standard A_ij generate PB_n
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥1, PB_n is generated by the geometric pure braids A_ij with 1≤i<j≤n; for n=1 the empty family generates the trivial group. This asserts generation, not a presentation or a list of relations.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on n. PB₁=1 by the published definition. Under the split forgetting map, A_in for i<n freely generate the kernel by the preceding lemma. For i<j<n, deleting the last strand leaves the same A_ij in PB_{n−1}; the chosen far-right section is geometrically the inclusion of the first n−1 braids with a stationary terminal strand, after the explicit basepoint path. By induction these older A_ij generate a subgroup mapping onto PB_{n−1}. Given β∈PB_n, express its image using older generators, lift that word, and multiply by its inverse to land in the free kernel, where the A_in generate. This proves generation without invoking later braid combing or Artin presentation completeness.

items.title: Pure braid groups are torsion-free
items.statement: Assume AC. For every n≥0, PB_n is torsion-free.
items.proof_strategy: PB₀ and PB₁ are trivial by the published definition. Suppose PB_{n−1} is torsion-free and g∈PB_n has finite positive order. Its image under forgetting has finite order and therefore is the identity; exactness puts g in the embedded free group F_{n−1}. The published free-group torsion theorem makes g the identity. Induction gives every n. Do not infer torsion-freeness of the full braid group from its finite quotient, and do not rely on a theorem about torsion in arbitrary K(π,1) groups.

title: Pure Braids, Fadell–Neuwirth, and Asphericity — Examples

items.title: The two-strand pure braid group is infinite cyclic
items.statement: Assume AC. PB₂≅Z, generated by the geometrically positive two-strand full twist A₁₂=σ₁². Under the published inverse-slicing identification its ordered-configuration winding is −1 relative to the counterclockwise meridian.
items.proof_strategy: At n=2 the exact sequence has quotient PB₁=1, so PB₂ is the free group on the one meridian of int D² minus q₁. The standard-generator definition gives A₁₂=σ₁², and the kernel-basis lemma identifies its ordered-configuration loop with the clockwise meridian. The wedge-of-one-circle computation identifies the free group with Z; counterclockwise winding gives A₁₂ value −1, or equivalently the isomorphism chosen to send A₁₂ to +1 uses the opposite orientation.

items.title: PB₃ as F₂ by Z, with its section action
items.statement: Assume AC. With a=A₁₂, b=A₁₃, c=A₂₃ and the far-right section that fixes the third point on a small representative of a, PB₃≅⟨b,c⟩⋊⟨a⟩≅F₂⋊Z. Writing w=bc, the action of the positive generator a is x↦w^{−1}xw on x∈F₂, for this section and the first-under-second convention. This does not assert a direct-product decomposition.
items.proof_strategy: The exact kernel has free basis b,c and the quotient PB₂ has generator a. Choose the far-right section at a real standard basepoint; for a supported two-point full twist it keeps the third point fixed, so its lift is a. In the geometric braid group put s=σ₁ and t=σ₂. The definitions give a=s², b=ts²t^{-1}, c=t². Multiply to obtain abc=s²ts²t=(st)³=Δ² with Δ=sts=tst. The published three-strand relation implies Δs=tΔ and Δt=sΔ, hence Δ² commutes with both s and t; this is a direct rank-three calculation, not an invocation of the later center theorem. Thus z=abc is central and a=z(bc)^{-1}, so a x a^{-1}=(bc)^{-1}x(bc) for x=b,c, and then for all x in F₂. Record that another section changes the action by an inner automorphism; do not silently call this semidirect product direct.

items.title: Standard A_ij as point pushes after relabeling
items.statement: Assume AC. For every i<j, the standard pure braid A_ij is the closed-disc image of the one-coordinate motion that moves q_j clockwise around q_i along the compatible standard stem transported from the adjacent stem by H_{j-1}∘…∘H_{i+1}. Relabeling coordinate j as the terminal coordinate carries this class to the corresponding terminal-fibre loop at the permuted basepoint. For i<n, the braid-to-mapping-class isomorphism sends A_in to the point push of the clockwise terminal-coordinate meridian; the raw ordered slice of W_in is counterclockwise and the configuration identification inverts it.
items.proof_strategy: Use the kernel lemma’s terminal-coordinate meridian formula and its local winding and typed point-push naturality. The inverse-braid calculation identifies any one-coordinate motion with its point push; conjugation by H_{j-1}∘…∘H_{i+1} transports the adjacent point push and its compatible stem. Compare the two images under the braid-to-mapping-class isomorphism to prove equality, then use the commuting coordinate-permutation/open-to-closed square for the relabeled form. Derive the terminal sign by equating and inverting the kernel-lemma and configuration formulas. The argument makes no fibre-inclusion injectivity claim.

items.title: A torsion-free kernel and finite quotient can have a torsion middle group
items.statement: Assume AC for the cited pure-braid torsion theorem. The short exact sequence 1→PB_n→B_n→S_n→1 alone does not imply that B_n is torsion-free: a general short exact sequence with torsion-free kernel and finite quotient can have torsion in its middle group.
items.proof_strategy: Give the explicit generic sequence 1→Z→Z×C₂→C₂→1, where m↦(m,0) and projection is onto C₂. Check kernel, injection and surjection directly. The kernel Z is torsion-free, the quotient C₂ finite, but (0,1) in the middle has order two. The published braid-to-symmetric exact sequence and preceding pure-braid torsion theorem have exactly these two abstract features, so those features alone cannot establish torsion-freeness of B_n. Make no claim that B_n itself has torsion.
